static_traits.name: Pan Qi
static_traits.occupation: Holds three jobs at the same time
static_traits.marital_status: Proposed to girlfriend of three years (unmarried)
static_traits.social_status: Has close friends to talk to, but has not yet discussed her inferiority and anxiety with them; work pressure and wedding-proposal preparations have affected the relationship with her partner
static_traits.medical_history: Without major physical illness; has not yet experienced similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative; neutral tone, capable of self-reflection; marked self-criticism, often using 'should' phrasing; presenting catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and black-and-white cognitive tendencies in piano-practice scenarios

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling inadequate and inferior about musical ability (especially guitar); repeatedly frustrated when practicing new songs, even believing she will never become a good musician.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeks counseling out of awareness that this inferiority is affecting self-esteem and overall well-being, hoping to improve this state.

core_beliefs: I will never become a good musician

special_situations.event: Not yet able to play two new songs smoothly in practice this week
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even practice two songs well, it means I am destined never to become a good musician
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Watches tutorials and practices daily; when frustrated, sometimes forces continuing, sometimes simply stops practicing to avoid more sense of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never become a good musician

special_situations.event: Mistakes and stumbles when practicing a new song
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should be able to play well right now; if I am still making mistakes, it means I am terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pressures and criticizes oneself to promote progress; if pressure is too great, avoids or interrupts practice
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why can I not do it yet? I should be better by now

special_situations.event: Began practicing under high pressure of three jobs and preparing a marriage proposal
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot handle work, relationships, and piano practice all at once, it means I am overall no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to push through and keep practicing to prove oneself; choosing to avoid or stop when the pressure is too great
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is too much; I cannot do anything well

special_situations.event: Friends affirm her playing, but she recalls the frustration of learning new songs more strongly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any difficulty means overall inadequacy; good performances are not representative
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or downplaying positive feedback, fixating only on error and failure fragments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good performances do not count; what really matters is my failures

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a capable musician and to maintain competence and worth in front of important others
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying about disappointing herself and her partner
defense_goal: Reducing exposure to failure through self-criticism and avoidance, maintaining safety and self-protection

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough beginner prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges (internalized high standards and critical voice)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes her successful segments or positive feedback and invites her to acknowledge her ability
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously feels this positive evidence contradicts her 'I am not good enough' inner narrative, feeling demanded to 'whitewash reality'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reflecting her feelings in a gentle, supportive tone; not confronting her narrative, first empathizing with her anxiety, then inviting her to concretize positive evidence in small steps. Avoid direct correction; use open-ended questions and concretizing guidance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes structured practice and a recording plan and asks her to test her beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feeling demanded to prove herself; if she cannot, she will be judged; thus postponing or downplaying tasks citing external pressures (work and proposal preparations)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintaining a neutral, non-judgmental tone, acknowledging her objective load; helping break tasks into smaller achievable units, using co-formulating and choice-offering phrasing, emphasizing options and rhythm, reducing the sense of being controlled.

manifestations: Juggling three jobs and proposal preparations, subjectively experiencing 'being crushed by responsibility'
When practicing piano, held hostage by the rule 'should be better', feeling my space for self-choice shrinking
outcomes: Anxiety and a sense of unbearable burden

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Self-demands such as 'I should be better' and 'I should have mastered it by now' frequently appear in one's language
Using zero mistakes and quick mastery as the standard for self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to express behavior or needs outward, turning it toward herself instead, redirecting outward energy against the self, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Stopping practice when frustrated, turning criticism and pressure toward oneself (self-blame and shame)
Not expressing inadequacy and anxiety to friends, choosing to bear it alone

exception_events.target_problem: When trying to learn new guitar pieces, the client usually feels anxious and engages in self-denial (e.g. 'I will never become a good musician'), sometimes interrupting practice as a result.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When playing familiar songs, experiencing smooth playing and confidence; friends praise her performance and say they like listening to her play.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the piece difficulty matches proficiency, with prior mastery experience; receiving others' positive feedback and support reduced anxiety and enhanced competence.

positive_force: Has actions for practice and self-improvement (watching tutorials, practicing daily)
Friends' positive feedback and potential support network
Willing to try new methods and self-observation (open to behavioral experiments)
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and black-and-white thinking
Heavy external pressure (three jobs and preparing a marriage proposal)
Tends to avoid or stop practicing when frustrated
Sleep and diet affected, leading to decreased energy and resilience
Not expressing troubles to family or friends; channels for support not yet fully utilized

target_behavior.behavior: Anxiety and interrupted practice when learning new pieces
antecedent: Mistakes or stumbles when practicing a new song
High external stress (holding three jobs at the same time plus proposal preparations)
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing one week of failure, overgeneralizing as 'never any good', with decreased attention and tolerance under heavy resource load.
target_behavior.function: Escaping feelings of failure and anxiety-related discomfort, briefly reducing stress (negative reinforcement).
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased practice time and quality, lowered confidence and impaired self-esteem, further reinforcing the 'I am no good' belief, affecting sleep and diet, and spilling over into work and relationships.

target_behavior.behavior: Self-critical inner speech (such as 'I should be better', 'I am so terrible')
antecedent: Not yet mastering new pieces within the expected time
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected high standards and conditional worth: equating performance with self-worth, using 'should' rules to maintain control.
target_behavior.function: Trying to boost performance through self-pressure (the surface goal), while actually maintaining negative schemas and anxiety levels.
target_behavior.consequence: Rising anxiety and decreased motivation, increasing the likelihood of avoidance and interrupted practice, impairing overall well-being.
